title: Cross-region, capacity-aware variant substitution playbook for version-locked models
creator: Ethan Chen
description: Define and implement a production-safe policy and orchestration playbook for substituting requests when a customer pins to a specific model version (version-locked models). The goal is to allow graceful, auditable substitutions across regions and model variants when the pinned version is unavailable, degraded, or deprecated while respecting latency SLOs, cost constraints, and compatibility guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine supports region-aware substitution with a configurable priority list per customer
Substitution decisions include capacity cost estimate and telemetry gating before execution
Canary substitutions run with probabilistic routing (0-20%) and automatic rollback on signal breach
Deprecation flows trigger staged substitution with customer notification and audit log entries
E2E test harness demonstrates regional warmup and steady-state latency within 10% of baseline for substituted requests
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Design review and security sign-off (confluence spec)
Phase 1: Implement policy configs + compatibility scoring in routing service
Phase 2: Add telemetry gating and canary probabilistic sampler (0.1% -> 5% -> 20%)
Phase 3: Regional warmup job to pre-load KV cache and prime variants
Phase 4: Beta with 2 internal customers and one low-QPS public customer
Phase 5: Incremental rollout to all pinned customers with opt-out flag
telemetry_signals: p99 latency increase > 30ms on substituted requests
token cost delta > 15% compared to baseline
model quality regressions detected by automated eval set (BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-similarity threshold)
test_plan: Unit tests for policy precedence (region -> variant -> model family)
Integration test: routing service simulates partial regional outage and validates substitution path
Canary experiment harness to validate telemetry gating and rollback behavior
Chaos test: induce KV cache cold starts and measure warmup duration and latency impact
Customer-simulated regression tests using representative prompts and evaluation harness
notes: We must avoid automatic substitution for customers with strict model audibility/legal hold; add an opt-out label 'no-auto-subst'
Compatibility score combines tokenizer parity, response-shape contract, and quantization-sensitivity; threshold currently proposed at 0.85
